entities.summary: Bodhiruci (b. 450 CE) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Global. He was a prominent figure in the philosophical circles of ancient India and was known for his contributions to the development of Buddhist philosophy. Bodhiruci's ideas influenced various schools of thought, including Mahayana Buddhism and Hinduism. His works were widely studied and disseminated throughout the ancient world, shaping the intellectual landscape of the region. Bodhiruci's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the transmission of Buddhist philosophy from India to China, where it would go on to have a profound impact on the development of East Asian Buddhism. He is also notable for his involvement in the translation of Buddhist scriptures, which helped to spread Buddhist knowledge throughout the ancient world. Bodhiruci's legacy extends beyond his own era, as his ideas and writings continue to be studied and debated by scholars today. One of his most famous works, the Bodhiruci Sutra, is still studied and revered by Buddhist scholars today. The Bodhiruci Sutra is a central text in the development of Mahayana Buddhism, and its teachings on the nature of reality and the path to enlightenment continue to inspire and guide Buddhist practitioners around the world.
